[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard provides guidance on implementing event batching strategies in .NET 8 applications to optimize throughput and reduce network overhead when consuming or publishing high-volume event streams.
page_texts.5:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#scope]

### Scope

**In Scope:**
- Producer-side batching strategies with Confluent.Kafka
- Consumer-side batch processing patterns
- Batch size configuration and tuning
- Performance optimization techniques
- Error handling for batch operations

**Out of Scope:**
- Basic Kafka producer/consumer implementation (see STD-APP-EVT-001, STD-APP-EVT-002)
- Infrastructure-level throughput optimization (see Infrastructure standards)
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Guidance** - Batching is an optimization technique applicable when:
- Processing high-volume event streams (>1000 events/second)
- Network latency is a bottleneck
- Throughput optimization is prioritized over low latency
- Downstream systems support batch operations
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

Event batching provides:
- **Improved Throughput**: Process multiple events in single operation
- **Reduced Network Overhead**: Fewer roundtrips to Kafka brokers
- **Cost Optimization**: Lower AWS MSK request charges
- **Resource Efficiency**: Better CPU and memory utilization

**Related Documents:**
- **Pattern**: [PTN-APP-EVT-001 - Application Event Batching Pattern](../../../patterns/application/event-driven/PTN-APP-EVT-001-application-event-batching-pattern.md)
- **Standard**: [STD-APP-EVT-001 - Kafka Consumer](STD-APP-EVT-001-dotnet-kafka-consumer.md)

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#guidance]

### Guidance

**[GUID-EVT-005-001]** - **Producer Batching Configuration**
- Configure `LingerMs` (100-1000ms) to accumulate messages before sending
- Set `BatchSize` (16KB-1MB) based on message size and throughput requirements
- Enable compression (`CompressionType = Snappy` or `Lz4`) for network efficiency
- Use `BatchNumMessages` to limit number of messages per batch
- Monitor producer metrics to validate batching effectiveness

**[GUID-EVT-005-002]** - **Consumer Batch Processing**
- Use `consumer.Consume()` with timeout to collect messages into batches
- Process batches as unit of work (e.g., bulk database insert, bulk API calls)
- Commit offsets only after successful batch processing
- Consider using `System.Threading.Channels` for efficient batch collection
- Implement graceful shutdown to process remaining batched messages

**[GUID-EVT-005-003]** - **Batch Size Tuning**
- Start with small batch sizes (10-50 messages) and increase based on monitoring
- Monitor consumer lag and adjust batch size accordingly
- Balance throughput vs latency requirements
- Consider downstream system limitations (database connection pools, API rate limits)
- Use adaptive batch sizing based on message arrival rate

**[GUID-EVT-005-004]** - **Error Handling**
- Implement partial failure handling (process successful messages, retry failures)
- Consider smaller batch sizes for error-prone operations
- Log failed batch items with sufficient context for troubleshooting
- Use dead letter queue for permanently failed messages
- Implement retry with exponential backoff for transient failures

**[GUID-EVT-005-005]** - **Memory Management**
- Set maximum batch size limits to prevent out-of-memory errors
- Use streaming processing for large batches instead of loading all into memory
- Monitor heap usage and garbage collection metrics
- Consider object pooling for high-frequency batch operations
- Implement backpressure mechanisms when processing cannot keep up

**[GUID-EVT-005-006]** - **Timeout Configuration**
- Set appropriate batch timeout values (typically 1-5 seconds)
- Balance between batch completeness and processing latency
- Implement partial batch processing when timeout expires
- Consider different timeouts for different message priorities
- Monitor timeout occurrences and adjust as needed

**[GUID-EVT-005-007]** - **Transactional Batch Processing**
- Use database transactions for batch inserts/updates
- Implement two-phase commit for distributed transactions (if required)
- Consider eventual consistency patterns instead of distributed transactions
- Ensure idempotency for batch operations in case of retries
- Use batch-level deduplication where appropriate

**[GUID-EVT-005-008]** - **Monitoring and Observability**
- Track batch size distribution (min, max, avg, p95, p99)
- Monitor batch processing time and throughput
- Alert on consumer lag increases
- Log batch processing metrics with OpenTelemetry
- Track partial failure rates and success ratios

**[GUID-EVT-005-009]** - **Performance Optimization**
- Use async/await for I/O-bound batch operations
- Parallelize batch processing where message ordering is not critical
- Consider using `Parallel.ForEachAsync` for CPU-bound processing
- Optimize database queries with bulk operations
- Cache frequently accessed reference data

**[GUID-EVT-005-010]** - **Order Preservation**
- Maintain message order within partitions when batching
- Process batches sequentially within same partition
- Use partition keys to ensure related messages are in same partition
- Consider message timestamps for ordering when processing out-of-order batches
- Document ordering guarantees for downstream consumers
page_texts.10:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#when-to-use-event-batching]

### When to Use Event Batching

**RECOMMENDED for:**
- ✅ High-volume event streams (>1000 events/second)
- ✅ Operations with high network latency
- ✅ Bulk database operations (inserts, updates, deletes)
- ✅ Batch API calls to external systems
- ✅ Analytics and reporting workloads
- ✅ Data synchronization between systems

**NOT RECOMMENDED for:**
- ❌ Real-time processing requiring low latency (<100ms)
- ❌ Critical operations requiring immediate processing
- ❌ Simple transformations with no I/O operations
- ❌ Low-volume event streams (<100 events/second)
- ❌ Operations requiring strict ACID transactions
- ❌ Systems with limited memory for buffering
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

**Batch Collection:**
- Use bounded collections to prevent memory exhaustion
- Implement timeout-based flushing for incomplete batches
- Consider message priority when batching
- Preserve message metadata (headers, timestamps, keys)

**Error Handling:**
- Separate successful and failed messages in batch
- Implement item-level retry for failed messages
- Use circuit breakers for downstream system failures
- Log detailed error information for troubleshooting

**Performance:**
- Profile batch processing to identify bottlenecks
- Use connection pooling for database operations
- Implement caching for reference data lookups
- Consider parallel processing for independent messages

**Testing:**
- Test with various batch sizes (1, 10, 100, 1000+ messages)
- Test partial failure scenarios
- Test timeout behavior with slow processing
- Load test with expected production volumes

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#use-case-assessment]

### Use Case Assessment

Before implementing batching, assess your use case:

**When Batching is APPROPRIATE:**

| Use Case | Characteristics | Batch Size Recommendation |
|----------|----------------|--------------------------|
| **Claims Processing** | High volume, database writes | 100-500 |
| **Member Data Sync** | Periodic bulk updates | 500-1000 |
| **Analytics Pipeline** | Aggregation, reporting | 1000-5000 |
| **Audit Log Ingestion** | Write-heavy, low latency tolerance | 100-500 |
| **Data Migration** | One-time or periodic transfers | 1000-10000 |

**When Batching is NOT APPROPRIATE:**

| Use Case | Reason | Alternative |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| **Real-time Alerts** | Low latency requirement (<100ms) | Single message processing |
| **Payment Processing** | Transactional consistency required | Individual transactions |
| **User-facing APIs** | Interactive response time | Request-response pattern |
| **Critical Events** | Immediate action required | Event-driven individual processing |
page_texts.37:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#performance-validation]

### Performance Validation

Teams implementing batching should validate performance improvements:

**Baseline Metrics (before batching):**
- Messages processed per second
- Average processing latency
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, network)
- Consumer lag

**Target Improvements:**
- ✅ **Throughput**: 2-10x increase
- ✅ **Network efficiency**: 30-50% reduction in requests
- ✅ **Resource utilization**: 20-40% improvement
- ✅ **Consumer lag**: Maintained or reduced

**Load Testing:**
- Test with expected peak volumes
- Validate batch size under various loads
- Monitor memory usage during high throughput
- Test failure scenarios (partial batch failures)
page_texts.38:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

Teams implementing batching should monitor:

**Batch Processing Metrics:**
- Batch size distribution (min, max, avg, p95, p99)
- Batch processing time (p50, p95, p99)
- Messages processed per second
- Partial failure rate (%)
- Full batch failure rate (%)

**Consumer Health:**
- Consumer lag (messages behind)
- Offset commit rate
- Rebalance frequency
- Partition assignment stability

**Resource Metrics:**
- Heap memory usage
- GC collection frequency and duration
- CPU utilization
- Network throughput

**CloudWatch Alarms:**
- Consumer lag > 10,000 messages
- Batch processing p99 > 10 seconds
- Failure rate > 5%
- Memory usage > 80% of limit

**Operational Procedures:**
- Daily lag monitoring and trending
- Weekly performance review
- Monthly batch size optimization
- Quarterly capacity planning
page_texts.39:
[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#optimization-guidelines]

### Optimization Guidelines

**When to Increase Batch Size:**
- ✅ Consumer lag is consistently low (<1000 messages)
- ✅ Processing time is well under timeout
- ✅ Memory usage is comfortable (<60%)
- ✅ Downstream systems can handle larger batches

**When to Decrease Batch Size:**
- ⚠️ Consumer lag is increasing
- ⚠️ Processing time approaching timeout
- ⚠️ Memory pressure or OOM errors
- ⚠️ High partial failure rates

**When to Disable Batching:**
- ❌ Latency requirements not being met
- ❌ Complexity outweighs benefits
- ❌ Message volume doesn't justify batching
- ❌ Downstream systems don't support batch operations

[standards/application/event-driven/STD-APP-EVT-005-dotnet-event-batching.md#best-practices-summary]

### Best Practices Summary

**Do:**
- ✅ Start with small batch sizes and increase gradually
- ✅ Monitor batch processing metrics continuously
- ✅ Implement timeout-based flushing
- ✅ Handle partial failures gracefully
- ✅ Use bounded collections for backpressure
- ✅ Test with production-like volumes
- ✅ Document batch size decisions

**Don't:**
- ❌ Use batching for low-latency requirements
- ❌ Set batch sizes without testing
- ❌ Ignore consumer lag metrics
- ❌ Skip error handling for partial failures
- ❌ Commit offsets before successful processing
- ❌ Load entire batch into memory if very large
- ❌ Use batching without proper monitoring

### Performance Benchmarks

Based on internal testing with typical healthcare messages (2-5KB):

| Batch Size | Throughput (msg/sec) | Latency (p99) | Memory Usage |
|------------|---------------------|---------------|--------------|
| 1 (no batching) | 500 | 50ms | 100MB |
| 10 | 2,000 | 200ms | 120MB |
| 50 | 8,000 | 800ms | 180MB |
| 100 | 12,000 | 1.5s | 250MB |
| 500 | 18,000 | 4s | 450MB |
| 1000 | 20,000 | 8s | 800MB |

**Recommendations:**
- For low-latency requirements (<500ms): batch size 10-50
- For balanced throughput/latency: batch size 100-200
- For maximum throughput: batch size 500-1000
